newsitem.title: USA: Business group slams Treasury's Summers on remarks.
newsitem.headline: Business group slams Treasury's Summers on remarks.

text.p: A business lobby group on Wednesday criticized Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers for alleged "divisive rhetoric" on estate taxes that it said showed insensitivity to small businesses.

The National Association of Manufacturers said Summers' remarks on Monday that efforts to repeal estate taxes were motivated by "selfishness" showed lack of understanding for the problems the taxes can cause.
"The continued shortsightedness of the Clinton administration in tax matters is a growing frustration to the business community," NAM Vice-President Paul Huard said.

"Trying to preserve a family business from the ravages of estate taxes isn't selfishness, it's economic survival," Huard said in a statement. He said two out of three family businesses fail to survive in the second generation, primarily because of estate taxes that can reach 55 percent.
Summers on Wednesday retracted his comment about selfishness being a motivating factor for those who favored repeal, saying there was "room for honest disagreement."
But Summers added that he considered outright repeal of estate taxes "raises very important questions of cost and fairness" for the government in its revenue-raising efforts.
